mfa.title: Two-factor authentication

mfa.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
mfa.manual: Or enter this key by hand:
mfa.codesIntro: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe. Each works once instead of a code from the app, and they are shown only now. Your other sessions have ended.
mfa.removeWarning: Removing the authenticator lets your password alone sign you in, and ends your other sessions.
mfa.required: An organisation you belong to requires two-factor authentication. Set up an authenticator to continue.

routes.title: Routes
routes.intro: Each route publishes a private service on a gateway group, by hostname or by port.

route.title: Route {{name}} ({{type}})
route.notFound: This route does not exist, or you cannot see it.
route.noHostname: The gateway group has no public hostname, so only the port is shown.
route.setHostname: Set the names clients reach it by
route.mtu: UDP datagrams travel as QUIC datagrams up to about 1240 bytes, or 1412 bytes once path-MTU discovery has run. Larger ones go over the flow's stream: delivered reliably, but one late packet holds up those after it.
route.unverifiedTitle: HTTPS without checking the target's certificate
route.fallback: served over TLS and HTTP/2, the fallback for QUIC
route.changed: The route changed since this page loaded it. The page shows it as it is now; try again.
route.deleteAsk: Delete the route {{name}} with its hostnames, targets and port? This cannot be undone.
route.deletedNote: Its gateways stop serving it once they apply the change.

notServing.POLICY_INVALID: the connector's local policy does not load
notServing.PORT_IN_USE: the port is in use on the gateway
notServing.TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE: no data session over the route's transport
notServing.NO_DATA_SESSION: no data session to the connector
notServing.CAPABILITY_MISSING: its rpmgr release cannot carry out a feature the route uses; upgrade it
notServing.ownPort: {{target}} is one of rpmgr's own ports, which the all-in-one's connector never dials, whatever its policy allows. Point the target at the service itself.

preview.connectors: Connectors its streams would go to: {{names}}

targetForm.connectorNeeded: Choose the connector that reaches the target.
targetForm.unverifiedWarning: The gateway will not check the target's certificate. The traffic stays encrypted, but anyone on the network between the connector and the target can read and change it. Choose this only for a target whose certificate nothing can verify, such as a self-signed one.
targetForm.serverNameSentHint: Sent to the target; empty: the host's name.
targetForm.pinnedKey: Pinned public key, SHA-256 in hex
targetForm.trust: Trust the certificate it shows now
targetForm.trustNeeds: Choose the connector and enter the target's address first.
targetForm.trustFailed: The connector could not read the target's certificate: {{message}}

targetForm.proxyTCPOnly: TCP connections only; UDP datagrams get no header.
targetForm.priorityHint: Lower is preferred. A higher priority, on any connector, is a failover; one priority is shared by weight.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.intro: Connectors run next to private services and carry their traffic to the gateways.
connectors.builtInHint: The all-in-one's own agent: it runs in the controller's process and cannot be decommissioned. Switch it off instead.
connectors.notFound: This connector does not exist, or you cannot see it.
connectors.controlUp: Control session up from {{addr}}, last seen {{when}}.

transportSetting.AUTO: QUIC, falling back to TLS and HTTP/2

connectors.noRoutes: No route has a target on this connector.
connectors.changed: The connector changed since this page loaded it. The page shows it as it is now; try again.
connectors.decommissionWarning: Decommissioning {{name}} revokes its identity and ends its sessions for good; it cannot enroll again with it. Its route targets are deleted.
connectors.decommissionRoutes_one: This route has no other target and is deleted with it, which frees its port or hostnames: {{routes}}.
connectors.decommissionRoutes_other: These {{count}} routes have no other target and are deleted with it, which frees their ports and hostnames: {{routes}}.
connectors.decommissionRoutesFailed: The routes could not be read, so it is not known which of them would be deleted with it. Reload the page to try again.

enroll.title: Enroll a connector
enroll.ephemeral: Ephemeral: removed 30 minutes after it last disconnects
enroll.uses: Enter a whole number, 0 for any number.
enroll.targetsHint: One per line: an address or subnet with an optional port or port range, such as 10.0.0.5:5432, 10.0.0.0/16 (all ports) or 127.0.0.1:200-500, IPv6 in brackets, or a socket path. The installer writes them into the host's local policy; without any, the connector reaches nothing until one is allowed.
enroll.denied: Targets the connector must not reach
enroll.deniedHint: Optional, one per line in the same form. They win over the allowed targets: with 127.0.0.1:200-500 allowed, 127.0.0.1:345 still refuses port 345.
enroll.step2: 2. When the installer asks for it, paste this token. It is shown only now.
enroll.note: The token is never part of the command line, and it expires in {{lifetime}}.
enroll.waiting: Waiting for the connector to enroll and connect…
enroll.noTokens: No enrollment token can enroll a connector now.

gateways.title: Gateway groups
gateways.intro: Gateway groups take public traffic and pass it to the connectors.
gateways.noGroups: The org has no gateway group yet.
gateways.notFound: This gateway group does not exist, or you cannot see it.
gateways.changed: The gateway group changed since this page loaded it. Reload the page to see it as it is now, then try again.
gateways.hostnamesHint: One per line: the names public traffic reaches the group's gateways by.
gateways.cidrsHint: One CIDR per line: proxies in front of the gateways whose X-Forwarded-For the gateways keep.
gateways.noGateways: The group has no gateway yet.

gwActions.endpointsHint: One host:port per line: where connectors reach this gateway, its own address, not the group's.
gwActions.drainHint: Stops new public connections, and ends the open ones after the gateway's drain period.
gwActions.tokenIntro: A token that enrolls {{name}} and nothing else, valid for 1 hour. Making it needs you to confirm it is you.
gwActions.decommissionWarning: Decommissioning {{name}} revokes its identity and ends its sessions for good; its tunnel endpoints stop serving.

gwPages.title: Pages
gwPages.intro: The pages the group's gateways show browsers: built in, or your own complete HTML of at most 64 KiB. Your page runs no script and loads nothing from elsewhere; put styles and images (as data: URLs) into the page itself.
gwPages.tooLarge: The file has {{size}} bytes; a page has at most 65536.
gwPages.ask: Go back to the built-in page {{page}}?

pools.title: Port pools
pools.none: The group has no port pool: TCP and UDP routes have no public ports.
pools.range: Ports are 1 to 65535, the first no larger than the last.
pools.quotasIntro: How many ports of the group's pools the org's routes may hold. Empty: the pools alone limit them.

domains.title: Domains
domains.intro: Routes may use a hostname only under a domain the org has proved is its own. The org's certificates and CA bundles are here too.
domains.none: The org has no domain claim. Routes need a verified domain for their hostnames.
domains.method: How to prove it is yours

methods.http: An HTTP token, served by your gateways

domains.txtHow: Create this TXT record at your DNS provider, then check now:
domains.httpHow: Point the name at one of the org's gateways; they serve the token at {{url}}. Then check now. The token is:

pem.file: Or read it from a file:
pem.fileSecret: Or read it from a file; it stays in this page until you send it:

certs.title: Certificates
certs.none: The org has no certificate yet. HTTP routes with ACME get theirs on their own.
certs.renewQueued: A renewal is under way already.
certs.acmeKept: ACME manages it; it cannot be removed.

bundles.title: CA bundles
bundles.intro: The CAs that HTTPS targets verify their upstreams with.
bundles.none: The org has no CA bundle. HTTPS targets are verified with the system's roots unless they name one.

policies.title: Access policies
policies.intro: Who may reach a route and how often: by address, with a password on HTTP routes, and at a rate per client.
policies.none: The org has no access policy.

summary.rateLimit: rate limit: {{perSecond}} a second per client, {{burst}} at once

policies.denyWins: A deny rule wins: an address it matches is refused, whatever allows it.
policies.perSecond: Requests or new connections a second
policies.oneRateLimit: A policy has at most one rate limit.
policies.rateLimitBounds: A rate limit takes whole numbers from 1 to 10000, a second and at once; an empty burst is a second's worth.
policies.rateLimitHelp: Each client address, or IPv6 /64, on each gateway: HTTP requests, new connections or new UDP flows. Over it, HTTP gets 429, TCP is reset and UDP dropped. An empty burst is one second's worth.

routePolicies.title: Access policies
routePolicies.none: The route applies no access policy: every client reaches it.
routePolicies.denyWins: A deny rule of any policy wins over every allow rule.

review.banner: The instance is in restore review since {{since}}: the restore could not prove that every revocation since the backup was applied again.

review.orgIntro: A restore on {{since}} could not prove that every revocation since its backup was applied again. Check the members and roles below, and remove or downgrade anyone who should not have access. Resume only the API tokens you trust. Then confirm: until then the organisation is read-only.
review.orgReadOnly: This organisation is read-only since the restore on {{since}}, until its Owner confirms its members and roles, or the Instance Admin on the controller host with
review.noTokens: No API token of this organisation is suspended.
